subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir stopped counting steps because counting had started to feel like superstition, as if he were measuring distance against the possibility of failure.
source_quote: I had stopped counting the steps somewhere around the third hour of climbing — not because I lost track, but because counting had started to feel like superstition, like I was measuring the distance against the possibility of failure.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had been thinking about the Overbright intermittently for months, not with anticipation but like a theory he had not yet been able to test.
source_quote: I had been thinking about this moment, intermittently, for months. Not with anticipation exactly — anticipation implies you trust the thing to happen. More the way you might think about a theory you have not yet been able to test.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had stopped trusting that the Overbright would be real.
source_quote: I had stopped trusting it would be real.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir felt the sunlight was a kind of violence, not pain, but the body registering that something fundamental had changed.
source_quote: what I felt when it touched my face was a kind of violence, or close to it. Not pain. Just the body registering that something fundamental had changed, the same way a deep-water creature might register the pressure dropping.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in sunlight.
source_quote: I knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a class on material impermanence taught by Brother Quellin or another monk with chalk dust on his robe.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Some form of material impermanence — I think it was Brother Quellin, or possibly the tall one whose name I never quite caught, the one who always had chalk dust on his robe. The transience of tools. The attachment to implements. Something about a bowl and an empty hand.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the monastery curriculum’s focus on non-combat topics had not worked itself out for him.
source_quote: It had not, in fact, worked itself out.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Glabbagool peering out of the bag of holding with wide, present eyes, observing the surface world with attention.
source_quote: There is no other word for it. He peered. He had not been in sunlight before. None of us were entirely sure what Glabbagool's eyes were, from a structural standpoint, but they were wide and present and sweeping across the surface world with an attention that made my own response to the Overbright seem, by comparison, measured.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir found Glabbagool’s curiosity toward the surface world admirable, though he would not say it out loud.
source_quote: I found that admirable in a way I was not going to say out loud.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted that Grygum was doing something with his hands that was probably prayer and probably sincere.
source_quote: Grygum was doing something with his hands that was probably prayer and probably sincere.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspected Daz was already drafting a journal entry.
source_quote: Daz was, I suspected, already drafting a journal entry.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that the decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz’s call, framed as a group discussion but pulled by Daz’s analytical gravity.
source_quote: The decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz's call, framed as a group discussion but with Daz's particular analytical gravity already pulling it toward a conclusion before the conversation began.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had no opinion on sword whisperers but noted the category and moved on.
source_quote: I had no opinion on sword whisperers. I noted the category and moved on.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembered Thorin’s serious belief in the existence of a sword whisperer for Dawnbringer.
source_quote: He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with the particular dwarvish seriousness that Thorin applied to things he actually cared about, which meant he believed this person existed and should be found.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew Grygum had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read and would treat Candlekeep as both research and pilgrimage.
source_quote: Grygum was the only one among us who had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read, and Candlekeep was going to be, for him, something between research and pilgrimage. He would look up the lore of Bahamut. He would pick up pamphlets. He would be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir agreed with the group’s decision to spend their gold on adventuring gear rather than business ventures.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought, as he stood at the tunnel’s mouth, that they had made it — and now there was everything else.
source_quote: I stood at the entrance to the surface world, squinting at a sky that went farther than anything I had navigated in months, and I thought: this is where we were going. We had made it. Now there was everything else.
